$description: Color-only overrides applied under [data-theme="dark"], per docs/06-theme.md's Light/Dark Structure. Lives in themes/ (not src/ directly) so the main build's directory-wide JSON merge in parser.ts doesn't fold these into the base color tree. Only color tokens are overridden — typography, spacing, radius, breakpoint, zIndex, and motion are shared, matching docs/06-theme.md's stated scope. Values follow Material Design's documented dark-theme conventions (the existing light palette is already Material-derived): --ds-color-primary-main and --ds-color-surface-main/--ds-color-surface-contrast reuse the exact values from docs/06-theme.md's own worked example; the remaining semantic colors (secondary, error, warning, success, info) use the equivalent Material 200-tone tint for the same reason primary does — legible on a dark surface without the contrast tokens needing per-color hand-tuning. All *-contrast tokens are set to a single near-black (#1A1A1A, matching the existing color.surface.contrast light value) since every *-main token above is now a light pastel, and black text is legible against all of them — a single deliberate value, not six independent guesses. border.main uses Material's standard dark-theme divider opacity (rgba(255,255,255,0.12)) rather than a hex color, which is why its type is still "color" despite not being a hex string — the validator only checks value/type presence, not hex format. Shadow overrides use reduced opacity for dark mode since light-colored shadows would be invisible against a dark surface — standard Material dark-theme convention.
